main_body: Wooden rack base/box holding three spears; the body is rows ~26-46, with a light wooden stripe at rows 27-29 and front slats below. The spear shafts are thin vertical details.
top_band: Rows 26-28 show a thin tan/orange band (about 2-3 rows) across the top of the box, but it is the same material as the front planks and reads as a plank edge, not a surface seen from above. There is no distinct foreshortened top.
evidence: Down the middle column: spear shaft to row 25, then a dark outline at row 26, a thin tan band at rows 27-28, then red-brown planks, dark gaps, and another plank section with a tan stripe at row 41. The horizontal bars are stacked front-face planks seen face-on. The spears stand behind the box with no visible top surface, no interior shown, and no horizontal beam top. This is a front elevation with a thin rim, not a 3/4 object.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown tint next to the wood, which fits the standard. The wood has about 4 tones (tan, orange, red-brown, dark brown) and some plank banding, with spear shafts that are mostly flat orange-brown strips. The spearheads have a few grey steps. It is thinner than the reference stall and well, which have scalloped roofs, stone shading and many more colours per tile. The large flat shaft areas and plain plank fills make it a little lower in density than the reference.
